tools.title: Integer Chips and the Number Line
tools.intro: Add and subtract integers two ways at once: jumps on a number line and positive and negative chips with zero pairs. See why subtracting is adding the opposite.
tools.description: Choose a and b from −10 to 10 and add or subtract. The number line shows the two jumps, the chips show zero pairs being removed, and subtraction is rewritten as adding the opposite. The distance between the two numbers is shown as |a − b|.
tools.discovery: Adding a positive number moves right and adding a negative number moves left. Opposites make zero pairs, so a + (−a) = 0. Subtracting is adding the opposite, a − b = a + (−b), and |a − b| is the distance between a and b.

tools.title: Circles: Circumference and Area
tools.intro: Roll a circle along a line to see why its circumference is π diameters, then cut it into sectors and rearrange them into a near-parallelogram to see why its area is πr².
tools.description: Set the radius and roll the circle out to measure its circumference against its diameter. Switch to the area model, cut the circle into 4, 8, 16 or 32 sectors, and rearrange them into a shape with base πr and height r. Exact answers in terms of π and with 3.14 are shown side by side.
tools.discovery: Every circle's circumference is π (about 3.14) times its diameter, C = πd = 2πr. Rearranged sectors approach a parallelogram with base πr and height r, so A = πr². Doubling the radius doubles C and multiplies A by 4.
